title: There is another similar software called CLO, what is the difference?
content: We have two different products called Marvelous Designer and CLO that have been specifically designed for the entertainment and fashion industries, respectively. While similar, CLO is equipped with additional features that are essential to fashion designers including avatar size adjustability and support for DXF-AAMA (drawing) files. On the other hand, Marvelous Designer including UV editor, sculpt mode Other features unique to CLO are: The ability to measure the avatar as a tailor would, tech pack (specifications) feature, diverse stitching visuals, and advanced CAD features. To learn more about CLO, please visit [www.clo3d.com](https://www.clo3d.com/)
content_description: Discover our specialized products, Marvelous Designer and CLO, tailored for the entertainment and fashion industries, with CLO offering advanced features crucial for fashion design.

title: Avatar Properties
content: ### Objective Set the Avatar's properties, such as skin style, eye direction, skin friction, and color of body elements. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ### ### Operation Set the Avatar's properties. When you select an avatar, its properties appear in the property window. **Avatar Properties** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number for the avatar. **Size** | Lists the size Preset chosen from the Avatar Editor. **Body Styling** | **Skin Style** (Ver. 2025.0) | Set the appearance of the avatar from presets or Customize You can manually set the color of hair, skin, underwear, eyebrows, eyes, and lips by clicking the Style Configurator button on the right. **Eye Control** (Ver. 2025.0) | **Horizontal** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes horizontally. **Vertical** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes vertically. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of meshes, a very high particle distance and a low Skin Offset value can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, as the simulation will slow down when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is in a stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (Ver. 2024.0 and above) | Apply a deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, Defualt Adult Avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: * When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. * Avatar-type objects that are not rigged can also be simulated. (2025.1) * NVIDIA GPU is supported starting from version 2025.2. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Divide Mesh** (Ver. 2025.0) | Subdivides the mesh of the avatars to smooth the surface of the avatar. Values are between 1 and 3. Use this feature only when necessary. The denser you set the mesh, the slower the simulation will run. E.g., This works best when you drape a fitted garment, such as leggings, since a low-density avatar mesh may be visible. **Material (Selected)** | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the selected part of the avatar. For Example: select the eyes and adjust color, base color map, etc. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of selected avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the selected mesh. **Avatar Properties (ver. 2024.2)** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. **Model** | You can change the type of avatar. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction when a garment is in stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (ver. 2024.0) | Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Material**(Selected) | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the avatar. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the mesh. **Smooth Avatar** | **Smooth** | Toggles the Smooth option on or off. If the option is on, the mesh on the avatar's surface will be divided as set in 'Division Level'. **Division Level** | Can be split by a factor of 1 to 5. **Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0)** **Soft Body for Custom Avatars (ver. 2025.1)**

title: UV EDITOR MODE: Edit UV location
content: UV Display UV Selection Arraying individual UV Arraying all UV UV Packing * * * ### UV Display (ver 2026.0) To control the UV display targets, click the UV Display icon in the UV Editor and select a display method. Refer to the following to select the UV display target: **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **UV Display Target** | **Show All Objects** | Displays the UVs of all garments and avatars in the scene. **Show Selected Objects** | Displays only the UVs of the selected garments and avatars. **※ Note:** The UV Display Element cannot be controlled when this option is activated. **UV Display Element** | **Show Garment** | Displays the UVs of garments. **Show Avatar** | Displays the UVs of avatars. * * * ### UV Selection UVs can be selected in several ways as described below. **Select All with Same Property** and **Select All Sewn Patterns** can be executed from the right-click pop-up menu of the selected UV. **Single Selection** | Click to select the desired UV. Hold Shift and click to add UVs to the previous selection. Multiple UVs can be selected by dragging. ---|--- **Select All with Same Property** | **Particle Distance** | Selects all Patterns that have the same particle distance. **Layer** | Selects all Patterns that have the same layer value. **Fabric** | Selects all Patterns with the same applied fabric. **Select All Sewn Patterns** | Selects all Patterns that have a direct or indirect sewing relationship with the selected Pattern. * * * ### Arraying individual UV #### Objective Arraying selected individual UV. #### Location Window ▶ UV editor mode ▶ UV right-click popup menu Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV right-click popup menu (ver. 2025.0) #### Operation Align | Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom | Selected UVs will be aligned by a selected standard. Align menu will be displayed when selecting more than two UVs. ---|---|--- Flip Horizontally | Selected UV will be flipped left and right. Flip Vertically | Selected UV will be flipped up and down. Fit UV to 0-1 | Selected UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. (ver. 10) * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. * * * ### Arraying all UV #### Objective Arraying all UV visible in UV editor mode. #### Location UV editor mode Right-click on background #### Operation Fit All UV to unified (0-1) | All UV will be aligned to 0-1 coordinates. Tile padding option Set the distance between the pattern and the outline in the dialog. * Length (Absolute): the actual distance * UV Coordinate (Relative): The ratio of 0-1 length to 1. The maximum distance is 0.4. ---|--- Set UV from pattern alignment | Location of all UV will be re-arranged as 2D pattern window. Zoom Extents All | Set the view in the UV window to reveal all patterns. (ver. 10) Show Wire | Disable texture and show mesh view. (ver. 9.5 below) * * * ### UV Packing #### Objective The selected UV shells can be automatically packed into the targeted UV tile. #### Location UV Editor ▶ Toolbar ▶ UV Packing #### Operation 1. Select desired UV shells to be packed. \- Ctrl+A can be used to select all existing UV shells. 2. Follow the dedicated path found in Location above to open Dialog box: Padding | Set the interval between UV shells. Unit: Permille (‰) of UV tile size. Min: 0.001 ~ Max: 0.999 ---|--- Packing Ratio (Archived since version 2024.1) | The percentage of area occupied by UV shells, compared to the size of the selected UV tile. Min: 80 ~ Max: 99 * 95% is the recommended input value. Higher values take more time to pack the UV shells. Fidelity (ver.2024.1) | The larger the value, the more sensitively the shape of the UV shell is calculated. Min: 1 ~ Max: 5 ![Fidelity.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438275643161) Fix Scale Ratio | Fix the current ratio of UV shells. Rotation | Allow UV shells to be rotated if needed. Advanced Placement (Ver. 2024.1) | Numerous sequences are tested to find a better placement to create least empty space. UV Area | Set the target UV tile to pack the selected UV shells. Reset | Reset all inputs in dialog box to default. Apply | All inputs will be applied to the UV shells and tiles. Close | Close the dialog box ※ Note: * When Advanced Placement is turned off, UV shells are placed sequentially from largest to smallest. * Advanced Placement option will decrease speed. Unless in extreme situations, it is recommended to turn Advanced Placement on.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance on managing UV displays, selections, arraying, and packing within the UV Editor for optimal textile design.

title: Quadrangular / Triangular Mesh
content: ### Objective Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures. ※Note: Please refer to the below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. As the program speed may differ due to their intrinsic characteristics, please select the most appropriate Mesh Type based on your needs. title: I have a verification issue. What should I do?
content: # **Objective** This FAQ will cover the trouble shooting for a verification issue. # **Details** Please use Chrome instead of other internet browsers. Marvelous Designer, and CLO-SET website is optimized as Chrome. **[CASE 1]** If you didn't receive the verification email, please check your spam mailbox. Sometimes the verification email can be found in your spam folder, or you will need to refresh your browser. **[CASE 2]** If Marvelous Designer web requires verification, even if you already verify it, please remove your old cookie and cache. **In Chrome** 1. On your computer, open Chrome. 2. At the top right, click More. 3. Click "Clear Browsing History". 4. Select a period on the top. To **delete** everything, select All time. 5. Activate the checkboxes next to "**Cookies** and other site data" and "**Cached** images and files". 6. Click Clear data. **[CASE 3]** Some school domains block external emails. If so, you can check your school domain is connected to the verification email on [Verify Email Address Link](https://www.verifyemailaddress.org/). If you see the result as "Connecting did not work", please ask your school admin (especially the technical division) to check if you could receive the verification email from Marvelous Designer. If you still have not received your verification email, please reach out to Marvelous Designer via [Contact Us](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/member/signin?returnpage=contact).
content_description: This FAQ page provides troubleshooting tips for resolving verification issues with the Marvelous Designer and CLO-SET websites, specifically optimized for Chrome users.

title: Trims
content: ### Objective Modify existing Trims and apply them to garments with the following features. * Glue Trim * Tack on Trim * Delete Trim * Transform Trims * Set Trim Stiffness * Right-Click Options Menu * Trim Simulation Recording ※Note: * To learn how to import OBJ as Trim, please refer to articles [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358223288601), [3D File (FBX) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017) and [Trim Style Window (Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) * To Learn and modify Trim Properties, please refer to the [Trim Properties](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187139609) page. * With the current versions, Trim Simulation with Collision only works with CPU Simulation. This does not work with GPU simulation at this time. * * * ## ## Glue Trim ### Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver 3.0.0). ### Operation #### Glue Trim 1. Click the loaded Trim with the Select/Move tool. → Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. 2. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. → preview tags along the mouse. 3. Click on the desired location. → Selected trim automatically attaches to the place. 4. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. ※ Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. 5. Activate Simulation. → Trim is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. ※Note: You can select multiple trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) * * * ## Tack on Trim (ver. 2025.0) ### Objective Attach trims to desired locations on by using the tack tool to apply them to multiple points across and various patterns. ### Operation 1. Using **Select/Move** tool in the 3D toolbar, click ![Direct Positiong.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438151583513)**Direct Positioning** next to the Gizmo. 2. Hover over the pattern and click the desired location. 3. Using **Tack** tool in the 3D toolbar, Click on an initial point on the trim. 4. Click on the desired point on the garment. * Repeat the step to tack the trim to multiple points 5. Click the Simulate tool. ※Note: Tack is not available on deactivated trims. * * * ## Delete Trim ### Objective Delete selected Trims ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport 2. Click Delete key on Keyboard to remove. → Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments. 3. Delete trim can also be done through the right click options menu. * * * ## Transform Trims ### Objective Transform trim as needed. ### Operation #### Via the Scale Gizmo Click and drag on the X, Y, or Z-axis to transform the Trim. Axis | Description ---|--- X-Axis | The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis | The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis | The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the along its z-axis. Square | The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. → The trim is transformed. When the trim transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. → The Gizmo used for moving and rotating trims appears. #### Via the Property Editor through [Trim Style Window](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim 2. Select the trim style to be transformed. → The properties of the trim appear in the Property Editor. 3. Find the Scale option. 4. Enter the desired value for the below options. Option | Description ---|--- X-Axis | Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis | Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis | Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio | Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. * * * ## Set Trim Stiffness (ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Semi-Elastic Trim can be achieved when reducing stiffness value. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D window. 2. In the Property Editor, adjust Stiffness Value. → When Stiffness Value is reduced, the trim will be slightly bent when sufficient force is applied. → To get more rigid Trim simulation, increase the Stiffness Value. ※Note: The Stiffness of the trim can only be set when the trim material is in the "active" state. * * * ## Right-Click Menu ### Objective Set extra Trim Options include Trim Simulation toggles, Unglue, refresh Trim Textures and export selected Trim to USD layer. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport. 2. Right-click on the selected Trim. → Trim is now being selected and Trim Options pop-up menu appears. #### Trim Options Select All Trims | Select all Trims in the 3D window. ---|--- Delete | Delete selected Trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Del Copy | Copy selected trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + C Paste | Pasted copied trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + V Simulation (ver. 2024.2) | Freeze | Freeze selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments but maintain the 3D position with no gravity influence. Activate | Activate simulation on selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments and influenced by weight and gravity. Deactivate | Deactivate selected trims. \- Trim does not collide with garments and maintains it’s 3D position. Unglue | Unglue trim from garment if glue function is applied. \- This option will not be available if glue function is not applied. Hide Trim | Hide selected trim or trims. Refresh Textures | Refresh selected trims textures. Export to USD Layer (ver. 12.1) | Export Trim to USD authoring layer, or create a new USD file with the selected trims. \- To learn more on USD export and USD layer editor in Marvelous Designer. Please move to [USD file Compatibility](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358343098777) page. ※Note: * To copy and paste multiple trims, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select all trims to be copied, then perform the procedure above. * When copying and pasting multiple trims, they must all be placed within a Pattern. * * * ### Trim Simulation Recording (Ver. 2025.0) When recording garment animation, the simulation cache of the Trim is recorded a separate layer from the Pattern, under the descendant of the Garment Layer.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for modifying and applying various trim features to garments, including gluing, tacking, deleting, transforming trims, and utilizing simulation tools for enhanced garment design.

title: VRM File
content: ## **Ver 2026.0** **** VRM file type is the most widely used 'universal format for 3D avatars' in the virtual metaverse. This is convenient 3D character file that allow you to import animation-style custom characters directly into the software without complex settings or conversion processes, enabling you to dress and fit garments while maintaining the character's unique appearance and movements. **※ No****te:** The VRM file format is based on glTF 2.0, and the properties that can be controlled in the Import/Export VRM dialog box are identical to those of **glTF 2.0**. ## **Import VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu** ▶ **File** ▶ **Import** ▶ **VRM** , specify the file path and name to display the Import VRM dialog. 2. Set the desired properties in the Import VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to load the file. #### ## **Export VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ VRM** , specify the destination path and file name to display the Export VRM dialog. 2. Set the properties in the Export VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to export the file. **※****Note:** A VRM file can only be exported if it meets the following two conditions: * The top-level parent of the export target's joint root must form a single hierarchy. * It must have a humanoid skeleton structure.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting VRM files, the leading universal format for 3D avatars in the metaverse, ensuring easy customization and integration of characters without complex processes.

title: I got H0040 “Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers” error.
content: The error occurs when the Server PC and the Client PC could not communicate with each other. To solve the problem, 1. Enter “services.msc” in the execution window. 2. Check if Sentinel Local License Manager is “getting started” in the service window. If the status is not “getting started”, click your right mouse button and choose “Start” then restart your computer. 3. If you still have the problem, check if the version of the HASP driver in the Server PC and the Client PC is the same. If they are different, make their version the same. You can get the version information from the image below. 4. If any of the above methods do not work, ask a network expert for help on how to communicate the status between ports such as Server and Client 5. Check if 1947 port is occupied by other services or not.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to troubleshoot communication errors between Server and Client PCs, ensuring a seamless connection for optimal performance.

title: Shirring and Crease Principle
content: ### Shirring principle In this course, we will explore the different types of shirring shapes based on fabric. In addition to the wrinkles generated by the default fabric, there are various types of wrinkles, such as narrow wrinkles and wide wrinkles. You can achieve the desired wrinkles by adjusting the Detail items in the Fabric Property, but it may be challenging for beginners. However, if you understand the differences in how each fabric forms wrinkles, you can easily create various styles of wrinkles. ### Crease principle In this course, we will learn about the shape of creases based on fabric. When fabrics are stretched or overlapped with each other, various creases are formed based on the type of fabric. Following the Shirring principle, you can refer to the creases made for each fabric and apply them to the clothes you plan to create in the future.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to understanding the shirring and crease principles in fabric manipulation, empowering users to create diverse styles of wrinkles and creases in their textile designs.

title: Register Accessory: Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat .zacs (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Register the Avatar's Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat as an accessory file (ZACS). ### Location Main menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Register Accessory ### Operation #### **OBJ production** When making OBJ accessories in other 3D programs (Maya, 3ds Max, etc.), please follow the requirements below. * Set the work environment of the 3D program. (Axis: Y-Up, Unit: Millimeter) * Create a Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat OBJ according to the avatar file: Avatar | Prepare an avatar suitable for the Hair/Shoes to be registered. Marvelous Designer's default avatar or user avatar can be used. ---|--- Mesh | For the sharp angular expression, add an edge to the mesh to be reliably simulated in the Marvelous Designer. Dummy Mesh | For complex areas (shoelaces, heels, etc.) where the faces come into contact, wrap in a transparent and flat dummy mesh. Make the spacing between dummy meshes smaller and more consistent than shoe meshes. ![afceb30d-87c7-4216-9e12-09d416d724ce.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438327939353) Mesh Name | Hair | hair Shoes | ![5f603b9a-10ee-4566-99cc-a65d8cfc67e2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438282741017) (shoes_r, shoes_l) Glasses | (glasses_r, glasses_l) Earring | (earring_r, earring_l) Hat | hat Materials | Apply separately, various materials (leather, metal, plastic, etc.) Even if the heel is the same material, it must be applied separately, and the order must be at the bottom. ![9f3cb925-9f44-46fd-9c50-28b412f6a1ec.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328277273)![25966d9e-df58-4556-9750-145229a14af1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328531481) * Set the transform properties. (Translate/ Rotation: All axes 0, Scale: All axes 1) ![512e752f-6fcf-4ab8-a1fa-2af6e68d2d83.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438333672089) * Export to FBX file. ※Note: * .obj files don't contain unit information internally * With autoscale enabled, software estimates units assuming human-sized objects * When using .obj files, remember and use the same unit setting during export and import * .fbx format stores unit information internally, making autoscale import work correctly ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328861593) #### **Registering Accessories** 1. Open the avatar file for the Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat to be registered to. ※ Note: It is recommended to review the placement of the (FBX) file (Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat) that is intended to be registered and check that the position with the avatar is correct before you register it as an accessory. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The Register Accessory window appears. 3. After setting the following options, click the Save button. **Basic** | **Rigging Type** (ver 2026.0) | Select whether the accessory to register is defined for the Marvelous Designer default Standard or if it utilizes a general Rigging method. ---|---|--- **Standard** | Registers accessories according to the types defined in the Marvelous Designer default avatar. **Rigged** | Registers rigged accessories without a specific type. When loading the file, joints with the same name as the avatar's will be automatically merged. **Accessory Type** | **Hair** | Select this option to register hair mesh. **Shoes** | Select this option to register the shoe mesh. **Glasses** | Select this option to register glasses mesh. **Earrings** | Select this option to register the earring mesh. **Hat** | Select this option to register the hat mesh. **Object** | Select the type of the object (file and pattern) to register. You can load and select objects in the 3D window and adjust their positions directly. **File** | **File** | Select the mesh file path to register. **Scale** | Select the scale unit from Auto Scale/mm (Default) / cm (DAZ Studio) / in / ft / m / 8ft (Poster) / 8.6 ft (Poster). **%** | Set the scale of the mesh file. **Axis Conversion** | Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. Check the Invert box to invert the direction. **Patterns** | Select materials to register as accessories. **Option** | **Mirror Creation** | If you register shoes and earrings, it automatically creates the opposite object. Inverted relative to the central axis of the avatar. **Thumbnail** | **Auto** | A thumbnail will be generated automatically. **Custom** | Select this to add a custom thumbnail image. → The save file window appears. 4. Set the file name and path. → It is saved as a Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat file (.ZACS). ※ Note: Make sure the mesh layer noted below has the correct nomenclature in Blender. The other names do not matter. Otherwise, you may encounter an error message that the name is wrong. #### **![mceclip0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438329008153)**

content: ### USD Import/Export ### Objective Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in USD file and they are compatible with other 3D software. ### Location #### USD Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD #### USD Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD ### Operation #### USD Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → Import USD window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### USD Import Detail Settings Scale | Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. ---|--- Move Garment to Start Position | Jump to the position of the start frame of the motion where the garment was loaded and move it. Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame. Transition Animation | A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motion’s first pose in stages, and is created when the avatar’s current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. #### USD Export 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD → Save File window appears. 2. Select desired location to store, and click Save. → Export USD window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### USD Export Detail Settings Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. ---|--- #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. | Image Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel ---|--- Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. ※ Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0) Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Animation | Entire Region: Save the recorded garment's animation entirely. Play Region Only: Only the garment animation in the play area is saved.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting garments in USD format using Marvelous Designer, ensuring compatibility with various 3D software.

title: Garment Fit Properties (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Change the range, unit, and appearance of Garment Fit Maps. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Garment Fit Properties ### Operation [**[PDF] Workflow guide**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358145161113) 1. Check the following before using Garment Fitting Maps: * Fabric: Apply the fabric type that is appropriate for the design. * Avatar: Use an avatar in the right size. Adjust an avatar size according to your measurement chart or fitting model in the Avatar Editor. Main Menu > Avatar > Avatar Editor > Avatar Size * Pose: Choose an avatar’s pose according to your style. Library > Avatar > choose the correct avatar version > Pose * Simulation: Change the Simulation Mode to Fitting (Accurate Fabric) or Animation (Stable) * Simulate every time after you change a design / fabric. 2. Open the Garment Fit Properties window from the Location above and modify its properties: **Fit Properties:** Properties | Description ---|--- Stress | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | kPa | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in kPa of the fabric that causes garment deformation. gf/cm2 | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in gf/cm2 of the fabric that causes garment deformation. mmHg | Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area in mmHg of the fabric that causes garment deformation. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. Face | The color map will be applied on the face of the garment. Point | The color map will be applied on the points of the mesh. Show | Select or deselect Weft / Warp / Shear to be included in the fit properties. Strain | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | % (percent) | The strain map is calculated through percentage. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. Face | The color map will be applied on the face of the garment. Point | The color map will be applied on the points of the mesh. Show | Select or deselect Weft / Warp / Shear to be included in the fit properties. Pressure | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | kPa | Displays the force per unit area in kPa applied to a garment by external stress. Represents the internal stress and tension in the fabric itself when stretched. gf/cm2 | Displays the force per unit area in gf/cm2 applied to a garment by external stress. Measures the actual pressure exerted by the garment on the body surface. mmHg | Displays the force per unit area in mmHg applied to a garment by external stress. Measures the compression pressure applied by the garment to the body. Color | Individually customize the color of the maps. Opacity | Individually adjust the opacity of the color. Graph Type | Gradation | The colors will be applied through gradation. Section | The colors will be applied through sections. Mesh | The color map will be applied on the lines of the mesh. Face | The color map will be applied on the face of the garment. Point | The color map will be applied on the points of the mesh. ※Notes: * Only one map can be activated at a time * When clicking on a point of a garment in the 3D window, the measurement appears. * Try to raise the percentage value for very stretchy fabrics and to lower percentage value for non-stretch / low-stretch fabrics to get more accurate results. It applies to all three Garment Fit Maps. * Blue (100%) shows areas where fabric is not stretched, while red shows the most stretched areas. Red areas in the Strain Map are not necessarily a critical issue, but they have to be investigated further by using the Stress Map. * Try different poses such as standing, sitting, or running for checking the fit of the garment.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for adjusting the range, unit, and visual properties of Garment Fit Maps to enhance garment fitting accuracy and customization.

title: ZIPPER: Registering Custom OBJ to Component
content: ### Objective Allows the user to create custom components for zippers that function dynamically in the 3D Window exactly as default provided zipper components. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper Tool ▶ Property Editor ▶ Type ▶ '+' ### Operation #### Workflow 1. Create mesh for Zipper Components(Puller, Slider, Teeth, and Stopper) export as an OBJ. → If creating a single OBJ file for both Slider & Puller, the node for the Slider must be named "Slider," and the node for the Puller must be named "Puller" before export. 2. Navigate to either of the locations listed above under "Location" and click on 'Register OBJ' or the '+' icon in the Property Editor. 3. Select the relevant Type (Slider, Puller, Slider & Puller, Teeth, Stopper). 4. In the File section of the Register OBJ dialog, click on the four-square button to navigate to the location of the custom OBJ file and Double-Click to select it. 5. Adjust the position of the Puller or Slider in the preview window. 6. Click 'OK'. 7. Load a garment with a Zipper. 8. Click on the Zipper in the 3D Window. 9. In the Property Editor for the Zipper, observe that the Slider, Puller, Teeth or Stopper the user has registered is now available to be assigned to the zipper. → You can find the custom Zipper component in the dropdown menu to the right of Slider or Puller under the 'Type' section. #### Options The options for the Register OBJ dialog are as follows. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Type** | Select the type (Slider, Puller, Slider & Puller, Teeth, and Stopper) to register the OBJ. **Name** | Enter a file name. **Scale** | Adjust the size of the OBJ. **Axis Conversion** | Change each axis of the OBJ. **File** | **OBJ** | Slider / Puller | Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) | Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider & Puller | Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Teeth (ver 2026.0) | Load the OBJ file to register as the zipper teeth. The spacing between the teeth is set to 0 mm by default. Adjust the spacing while previewing the result in the preview window. **Preview** | Check the imported OBJ file in advance. Space | When registering teeth, set the spacing for individual teeth objects. **Puller Position** | For Slider or Slider & Puller type. Adjust the sliders on the X, Y, and Z axes to set where the puller is attached.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to create and register custom 3D zipper components, enabling dynamic functionality in the 3D Window.

title: Linked Editing
content: ### ### ### Objective Copy and paste/mirror paste Patterns with Linked Editing function to edit them simultaneously. Or apply linked editing function to existing pair of symmetric Patterns (ver3.0.0). ### Location #### Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern #### Apply Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Apply Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern #### Remove Linked Editing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Remove Linked Editing ### Operation #### Clone Pattern with Linked Editing 1. Select the Pattern to be duplicated with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern 3. The clone of the Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. → Symmetric Patterns's outline is highlighted in light-blue (ver2.5.0). 4. Click on the 2D window to place the clone. → The selected Pattern is pasted/mirror pasted with Linked Editing function. ※ Note: When copying the Pattern as an instance (Instance Pattern,) right click on the 2D window to access the Paste window which allows you to set Interval and Number of Shapes. #### Apply Linked Editing 1. Select the patterns to be linked with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Apply Linked Editing ▶ Symmetric Pattern (With Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern/Instance Pattern → Selected Patterns are linked and can be edited simultaneously. #### Remove Linked Editing 1. Select the Patterns which the Linked Editing function should be removed with the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Remove Linked Editing → The applied Linked Editing function is removed.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to utilize the Linked Editing function for cloning and applying symmetric patterns, enabling simultaneous editing for enhanced design efficiency.

title: Flatten
content: ### Objective Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar. ※ Note: The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Flatten 3D Toolbar ▶ Flatten → Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. 2. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as a Pattern. → The area to be flattened appears in light blue. 3. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. → The selected areas are highlighted in yellow. 4. Press the Enter key to execute **Flatten (Separate)**. → The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. → The default Fabric is applied to all Patterns created with the Flatten tool. → Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. → The lines remain on the Avatar. 5. Press the Shift + Enter key to execute **Flatten (Merge)**. → If adjacent surfaces are selected, a single merged pattern will be created.
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for extracting patterns from an Avatar using the Flatten tool, detailing step-by-step operations for both separating and merging selected shapes.

title: Trace
content: ### ### Objective Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area to Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace ### Operation #### Trace as a Pattern * Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace * Select the Baselines to be traced. * Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. * Select Trace as a Pattern. →The selected Baselines are traced as a Pattern. **※ Note:** * Select the Internal Lines, or Outlines on both sides of the half-symmetry pattern. * The half-symmetry relationship on the newly traced pattern can be maintained. Internal lines and Baselines within the selection range are contained in the traced pattern. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56586935876889) #### Trace as an Internal Shape 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as an Internal Shape. →When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. #### Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. →The right click pop-up menu appears. 4. Select Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes. →The selected lines will be traced as they are. ※ Note: * To easily select a closed shape, double click on the Internal Line. * Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Trace function to convert lines, shapes, and areas into patterns within the 2D Pattern toolbar.
